title: Configure Solid Queue, Solid Cache and Solid Cable topology
summary: Activated Solid Queue and Solid Cache across Rails runtimes and Solid Cable in development/staging/production; added a single-source queue/priority registry, exact isolated worker role allowlists, scheduler ownership enforcement, bounded retry/discard behavior, safe recurring cleanup, disposable cache/cable limits, a real PostgreSQL smoke job and operational runbook.

tests.notes: 39 runs, 279 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips against four PostgreSQL databases

tests.command: RAILS_ENV=test ... bundle exec rails test test/jobs/solid_stack_topology_test.rb test/database/postgresql_configuration_test.rb test/configuration/configuration_test.rb

tests.notes: worker_default, worker_crawl, worker_render, worker_analysis, worker_report and scheduler all reported valid Solid Queue configuration
negative test exited 1 with exact allowed job-role list
negative test exited 1 before boot with clear required-role error

tests.notes: blueprint valid with 120 prompts and 10 ADRs
120 prompts; catalog and state consistent before completion

decisions: Use exact queue allowlists with no wildcard polling; isolate render to one thread per worker_render process; retain finished jobs for 24 hours to support recurring de-duplication; allow only the scheduler role to own recurring scheduling; treat cache and cable as disposable non-authoritative data
risks: Queue pool capacity still requires operators to count supervisor and forked actors when setting deployment-wide database budgets. Test keeps the Action Cable test adapter for deterministic assertions while development/staging/production use Solid Cable. Brakeman emitted non-fatal Ruby 3.4 parser/native-extension diagnostics but reported zero scanner errors and zero warnings. An initial RuboCop attempt could not write the user-level cache; the repeat with workspace RUBOCOP_CACHE_ROOT passed.
